quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The analyst said, 'The company's shares have fallen sharply this week.'
options: The analyst said the company's shares had fallen sharply that week.
The analyst said the company's shares fell sharply this week.
The analyst said the company's shares had been falling sharply that week.
quests.correctAnswer: The analyst said the company's shares had fallen sharply that week.
quests.sentence: The analyst said, 'The company's shares have fallen sharply this week.'
quests.hint: 'Have fallen' → 'had fallen'. 'This week' → 'that week'. The simple perfect is preserved.
quests.explanation: 'Have fallen' → 'had fallen'. 'This week' → 'that week'. Do not change the tense aspect from simple to continuous.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Does anyone know when the next train to Oxford departs?'
options: She asked if anyone knew when the next train to Oxford departed.
She asked does anyone know when the next train to Oxford departs.
She asked if anyone knew when the next train to Oxford departs.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if anyone knew when the next train to Oxford departed.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Does anyone know when the next train to Oxford departs?'
quests.hint: Both verbs shift: 'knows' → 'knew', 'departs' → 'departed'. Use 'if' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Does anyone know' → 'anyone knew'. The embedded verb 'departs' also shifts to 'departed'. Both verbs must shift.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The careers advisor said, 'Ensure your CV is tailored to each role you apply for.'
options: The careers advisor told graduates to ensure their CVs were tailored to each role they applied for.
The careers advisor told graduates to ensure their CVs are tailored to each role you apply for.
The careers advisor said ensure your CV is tailored to each role you apply for.
quests.correctAnswer: The careers advisor told graduates to ensure their CVs were tailored to each role they applied for.
quests.sentence: The careers advisor said, 'Ensure your CV is tailored to each role you apply for.'
quests.hint: Imperative with embedded passive clause and relative clause. All verbs and pronouns must shift.
quests.explanation: 'Ensure' → 'to ensure'. 'Is tailored' → 'were tailored'. 'Apply' → 'applied'. 'Your' → 'their'. 'You' → 'they'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I hadn't expected the project to be so challenging.'
options: She said she hadn't expected the project to be so challenging.
She said she didn't expect the project to be so challenging.
She said she hadn't been expecting the project to be so challenging.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she hadn't expected the project to be so challenging.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I hadn't expected the project to be so challenging.'
quests.hint: Past perfect 'hadn't expected' cannot shift further. It remains unchanged in reported speech.
quests.explanation: 'Hadn't expected' is already past perfect. In reported speech, past perfect does not shift further - it stays as 'hadn't expected'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The journalist asked, 'What steps are being taken to address the issue?'
options: The journalist asked what steps were being taken to address the issue.
The journalist asked what steps are being taken to address the issue.
The journalist asked what steps had been taken to address the issue.
quests.correctAnswer: The journalist asked what steps were being taken to address the issue.
quests.sentence: The journalist asked, 'What steps are being taken to address the issue?'
quests.hint: Present continuous passive → past continuous passive. Not past perfect passive.
quests.explanation: 'Are being taken' (present continuous passive) → 'were being taken' (past continuous passive). 'Had been taken' changes the aspect.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The editor said, 'Proofread everything twice before sending.'
options: The editor insisted we proofread everything twice before sending.
The editor insisted to proofread everything twice before sending.
The editor insisted that proofread everything twice before sending.
quests.correctAnswer: The editor insisted we proofread everything twice before sending.
quests.sentence: The editor said, 'Proofread everything twice before sending.'
quests.hint: 'Insist' takes 'that + subject + base verb' or 'on + -ing'. 'Insist to' is incorrect.
quests.explanation: 'Insist' can be followed by 'that + subject + verb (base form)': 'insisted we proofread'. 'Insisted to proofread' is grammatically incorrect.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'The results are more promising than we had expected.'
options: She reported the results were more promising than they had expected.
She reported the results are more promising than they had expected.
She reported the results had been more promising than they had expected.
quests.correctAnswer: She reported the results were more promising than they had expected.
quests.sentence: She said, 'The results are more promising than we had expected.'
quests.hint: 'Are' → 'were'. 'Had expected' stays. 'We' → 'they'.
quests.explanation: 'Are' → 'were'. 'Had expected' is already past perfect - it stays. 'We' → 'they'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He was asked, 'What would you do differently if you had the chance?'
options: He was asked what he would do differently if he had the chance.
He was asked what he would do differently if he had had the chance.
He was asked what would he do differently if he had the chance.
quests.correctAnswer: He was asked what he would do differently if he had the chance.
quests.sentence: He was asked, 'What would you do differently if you had the chance?'
quests.hint: Second conditional: 'would do' stays. 'Had the chance' stays. 'You' → 'he'. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Second conditional: 'would do' and 'had' do not shift further. 'You' → 'he'. 'Had had' would be an over-shift. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The therapist said, 'Focus on what you can control and let go of what you can't.'
options: The therapist advised patients to focus on what they could control and let go of what they couldn't.
The therapist advised patients to focus on what they can control and let go of what you can't.
The therapist advised patients to focus on what they could control and let go of what they can't.
quests.correctAnswer: The therapist advised patients to focus on what they could control and let go of what they couldn't.
quests.sentence: The therapist said, 'Focus on what you can control and let go of what you can't.'
quests.hint: 'Can' → 'could'. 'Can't' → 'couldn't'. 'You' → 'they'. Both embedded modals shift.
quests.explanation: Both 'can' and 'can't' shift to 'could' and 'couldn't'. 'You' → 'they'. Both modal verbs in the embedded clauses must be updated.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I know this will sound strange, but I think I've seen you before.'
options: She said she knew it would sound strange, but she thought she had seen me before.
She said she knows this will sound strange, but she thinks she's seen me before.
She said she knew it would sound strange, but she thought she had seen you before.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she knew it would sound strange, but she thought she had seen me before.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I know this will sound strange, but I think I've seen you before.'
quests.hint: Multiple shifts: 'know' → 'knew', 'this' → 'it', 'will sound' → 'would sound', 'think' → 'thought', 'have seen' → 'had seen', 'you' → 'me'.
quests.explanation: Six shifts: 'know' → 'knew', 'this' → 'it', 'will sound' → 'would sound', 'think' → 'thought', 'have seen' → 'had seen', 'you' → 'me'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The union representative asked, 'Were the changes introduced with sufficient notice?'
options: The union representative asked whether the changes had been introduced with sufficient notice.
The union representative asked were the changes introduced with sufficient notice.
The union representative asked whether the changes were introduced with sufficient notice.
quests.correctAnswer: The union representative asked whether the changes had been introduced with sufficient notice.
quests.sentence: The union representative asked, 'Were the changes introduced with sufficient notice?'
quests.hint: Past passive → past perfect passive. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Were introduced' (past simple passive) → 'had been introduced' (past perfect passive). Use 'whether' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The communication trainer said, 'Invest time in understanding your audience before presenting.'
options: The communication trainer told the group to invest time in understanding their audience before presenting.
The communication trainer told the group invest time in understanding their audience before presenting.
The communication trainer told the group to invest time to understand your audience before presenting.
quests.correctAnswer: The communication trainer told the group to invest time in understanding their audience before presenting.
quests.sentence: The communication trainer said, 'Invest time in understanding your audience before presenting.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + group + to + invest'. 'Understanding' is a gerund. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Invest time in understanding' → 'to invest time in understanding'. 'Your audience' → 'their audience'. 'To understand' breaks the 'in + -ing' pattern.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'Apparently, the CEO resigned this morning.'
options: She said that apparently the CEO had resigned that morning.
She said that apparently the CEO resigned that morning.
She said that apparently the CEO had been resigning that morning.
quests.correctAnswer: She said that apparently the CEO had resigned that morning.
quests.sentence: She said, 'Apparently, the CEO resigned this morning.'
quests.hint: 'Resigned' → 'had resigned'. 'This morning' → 'that morning'. 'Apparently' stays.
quests.explanation: 'Resigned' (past simple) → 'had resigned' (past perfect). 'This morning' → 'that morning'. 'Apparently' (adverb) is unchanged.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The professor asked, 'Which sections of the report do you find most convincing?'
options: The professor asked which sections of the report I found most convincing.
The professor asked which sections of the report do I find most convincing.
The professor asked which sections of the report I had found most convincing.
quests.correctAnswer: The professor asked which sections of the report I found most convincing.
quests.sentence: The professor asked, 'Which sections of the report do you find most convincing?'
quests.hint: 'Do find' → 'found'. 'You' → 'I'. Statement order. No over-shift to past perfect.
quests.explanation: Drop 'do'. 'Find' → 'found'. 'You' → 'I'. 'Had found' would be an over-shift for a general opinion question.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The coach said, 'Ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve.'
options: The coach encouraged athletes to ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve.
The coach encouraged athletes asking for feedback regularly and using it to improve.
The coach said ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve.
quests.correctAnswer: The coach encouraged athletes to ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve.
quests.sentence: The coach said, 'Ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'encouraged + athletes + to + ask... and use'. Gerunds after 'encouraged' are less natural here.
quests.explanation: 'Ask' and 'use' are imperatives → 'encouraged athletes to ask for feedback regularly and use it to improve'. Both use infinitive form after 'to'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I was told that the position has already been filled.'
options: She said she had been told that the position had already been filled.
She said she was told that the position has already been filled.
She said she had been told that the position was already filled.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she had been told that the position had already been filled.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I was told that the position has already been filled.'
quests.hint: 'Was told' → 'had been told'. 'Has been filled' → 'had been filled'. Both passives shift.
quests.explanation: Both passive verbs shift: 'was told' → 'had been told', 'has been filled' → 'had been filled'. The perfect passive in the embedded clause is also updated.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Have the relevant stakeholders been consulted?'
options: She asked whether the relevant stakeholders had been consulted.
She asked whether the relevant stakeholders have been consulted.
She asked have the relevant stakeholders been consulted.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked whether the relevant stakeholders had been consulted.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Have the relevant stakeholders been consulted?'
quests.hint: 'Have been consulted' → 'had been consulted'. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Have been consulted' (present perfect passive) → 'had been consulted' (past perfect passive). Use 'whether'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The dean said, 'Make the most of every learning opportunity.'
options: The dean encouraged students to make the most of every learning opportunity.
The dean encouraged students making the most of every learning opportunity.
The dean said make the most of every learning opportunity.
quests.correctAnswer: The dean encouraged students to make the most of every learning opportunity.
quests.sentence: The dean said, 'Make the most of every learning opportunity.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'encouraged + students + to + make the most of'.
quests.explanation: 'Make the most of' is an imperative → 'encouraged students to make the most of every learning opportunity'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The prosecutor said, 'The evidence strongly suggests the defendant was at the scene.'
options: The prosecutor said the evidence strongly suggested the defendant had been at the scene.
The prosecutor said the evidence strongly suggests the defendant was at the scene.
The prosecutor said the evidence strongly suggested the defendant was at the scene.
quests.correctAnswer: The prosecutor said the evidence strongly suggested the defendant had been at the scene.
quests.sentence: The prosecutor said, 'The evidence strongly suggests the defendant was at the scene.'
quests.hint: 'Suggests' → 'suggested'. 'Was' → 'had been'. Both verbs shift.
quests.explanation: Two shifts: 'suggests' → 'suggested' and 'was' → 'had been'. The embedded 'was' shifts to past perfect 'had been'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The investor asked, 'What makes this product different from your competitors'?'
options: The investor asked what made that product different from their competitors'.
The investor asked what makes this product different from your competitors'.
The investor asked what makes that product different from their competitors'.
quests.correctAnswer: The investor asked what made that product different from their competitors'.
quests.sentence: The investor asked, 'What makes this product different from your competitors'?'
quests.hint: 'Makes' → 'made'. 'This' → 'that'. 'Your competitors'' → 'their competitors''. Statement order.
quests.explanation: Three shifts: 'makes' → 'made', 'this' → 'that', 'your' → 'their'. Use statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The IT security expert said, 'Separate your personal and professional email accounts.'
options: The IT security expert advised users to separate their personal and professional email accounts.
The IT security expert advised users to separate your personal and professional email accounts.
The IT security expert told to separating personal and professional email accounts.
quests.correctAnswer: The IT security expert advised users to separate their personal and professional email accounts.
quests.sentence: The IT security expert said, 'Separate your personal and professional email accounts.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'advised + users + to + separate'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Separate' is an imperative → 'advised users to separate their personal and professional email accounts'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'I'm not sure I can trust what she's been telling me.'
options: He said he wasn't sure he could trust what she had been telling him.
He said he isn't sure he can trust what she's been telling me.
He said he wasn't sure he could trust what she was telling him.
quests.correctAnswer: He said he wasn't sure he could trust what she had been telling him.
quests.sentence: He said, 'I'm not sure I can trust what she's been telling me.'
quests.hint: 'Am not sure' → 'wasn't sure'. 'Can trust' → 'could trust'. 'Has been telling' → 'had been telling'. 'Me' → 'him'.
quests.explanation: Four shifts: 'am' → 'was', 'can' → 'could', 'has been telling' → 'had been telling', 'me' → 'him'. The perfect continuous is preserved.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The project manager asked, 'Was the original estimate accurate?'
options: The project manager asked whether the original estimate had been accurate.
The project manager asked whether the original estimate was accurate.
The project manager asked was the original estimate accurate.
quests.correctAnswer: The project manager asked whether the original estimate had been accurate.
quests.sentence: The project manager asked, 'Was the original estimate accurate?'
quests.hint: 'Was accurate' → 'had been accurate'. Use 'whether' and statement order.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'was accurate' shifts to past perfect 'had been accurate'. Use 'whether' for yes/no questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The mentor said, 'Revisit your goals quarterly to track your progress.'
options: The mentor told the mentee to revisit goals quarterly to track their progress.
The mentor told the mentee to revisit your goals quarterly to track your progress.
The mentor said revisit your goals quarterly to track your progress.
quests.correctAnswer: The mentor told the mentee to revisit goals quarterly to track their progress.
quests.sentence: The mentor said, 'Revisit your goals quarterly to track your progress.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + mentee + to + revisit'. 'Your goals' → 'goals'. 'Your progress' → 'their progress'.
quests.explanation: 'Revisit' → 'to revisit'. 'Your goals' becomes 'goals' (object known). 'Your progress' → 'their progress'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'It seems as though the issue has been resolved at last.'
options: He said it seemed as though the issue had been resolved at last.
He said it seems as though the issue has been resolved at last.
He said it seemed as though the issue was resolved at last.
quests.correctAnswer: He said it seemed as though the issue had been resolved at last.
quests.sentence: He said, 'It seems as though the issue has been resolved at last.'
quests.hint: 'Seems' → 'seemed'. 'Has been resolved' → 'had been resolved'. Passive perfect preserved.
quests.explanation: 'Seems' → 'seemed'. 'Has been resolved' (present perfect passive) → 'had been resolved' (past perfect passive).

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The marketing team asked, 'How satisfied are customers with the current service?'
options: The marketing team asked how satisfied customers were with the current service.
The marketing team asked how satisfied are customers with the current service.
The marketing team asked how satisfied customers had been with the current service.
quests.correctAnswer: The marketing team asked how satisfied customers were with the current service.
quests.sentence: The marketing team asked, 'How satisfied are customers with the current service?'
quests.hint: 'Are' → 'were'. Statement order. No over-shift to past perfect for a current process question.
quests.explanation: 'Are satisfied' → 'were satisfied'. Use statement word order. 'Had been' would be an over-shift for a question about a current, ongoing service.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The performance coach said, 'Focus on your strengths while working to improve your weaknesses.'
options: The performance coach advised the athlete to focus on strengths while working to improve weaknesses.
The performance coach advised the athlete to focus on your strengths while working to improve your weaknesses.
The performance coach said focus on your strengths while working to improve your weaknesses.
quests.correctAnswer: The performance coach advised the athlete to focus on strengths while working to improve weaknesses.
quests.sentence: The performance coach said, 'Focus on your strengths while working to improve your weaknesses.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'advised + athlete + to + focus'. Pronoun 'your' is dropped as the subject is now clear.
quests.explanation: 'Focus' is an imperative → 'advised the athlete to focus on strengths while working to improve weaknesses'. 'Your' is naturally dropped as the subject is clear.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The minister said, 'The new law will come into force next April.'
options: The minister announced the new law would come into force the following April.
The minister announced the new law will come into force next April.
The minister announced the new law would come into force in next April.
quests.correctAnswer: The minister announced the new law would come into force the following April.
quests.sentence: The minister said, 'The new law will come into force next April.'
quests.hint: 'Will come' → 'would come'. 'Next April' → 'the following April'. No 'in' before 'the following April'.
quests.explanation: 'Will come' → 'would come'. 'Next April' → 'the following April'. Adding 'in' before 'the following April' is unnatural.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Who is going to be in charge of the marketing campaign?'
options: She asked who was going to be in charge of the marketing campaign.
She asked who is going to be in charge of the marketing campaign.
She asked who would be going to be in charge of the marketing campaign.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked who was going to be in charge of the marketing campaign.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Who is going to be in charge of the marketing campaign?'
quests.hint: 'Is going to be' → 'was going to be'. Statement order. Avoid double modals.
quests.explanation: 'Is going to be' → 'was going to be'. Use statement word order. 'Would be going to be' is incorrect - do not combine 'would' and 'going to'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The public speaking tutor said, 'Speak clearly and maintain eye contact during your presentation.'
options: The public speaking tutor told students to speak clearly and maintain eye contact during their presentations.
The public speaking tutor told students to speak clearly and maintain eye contact during your presentation.
The public speaking tutor said speak clearly and maintain eye contact during your presentation.
quests.correctAnswer: The public speaking tutor told students to speak clearly and maintain eye contact during their presentations.
quests.sentence: The public speaking tutor said, 'Speak clearly and maintain eye contact during your presentation.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'told + students + to + speak... and maintain'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: Two imperatives → 'told students to speak clearly and maintain eye contact'. 'Your presentation' → 'their presentations'.
